slot.brief: Line through a point has given direction ratios; compute its direction cosines (with l²+m²+n²=1) or the angle with an axis.

stem: The direction cosines of a line whose direction ratios are $3$, $4$, $12$ are

verdicts.working: Normalize the direction ratios: \(\sqrt{3^2+4^2+12^2}=13\). Thus the direction cosines are \((3/13,4/13,12/13)\).

working:
Magnitude: $\sqrt{3^2+4^2+12^2} = \sqrt{9+16+144} = \sqrt{169} = 13$.
Direction cosines: $\left(\dfrac{3}{13}, \dfrac{4}{13}, \dfrac{12}{13}\right)$.

Independent check: Normalize the direction ratios: \(\sqrt{3^2+4^2+12^2}=13\). Thus the direction cosines are \((3/13,4/13,12/13)\).
solution: For direction ratios $(a,b,c)$, the direction cosines are $(a,b,c)/\sqrt{a^2+b^2+c^2}$. Here, $\sqrt{3^2+4^2+12^2}=13$, so the direction cosines are $\left(\dfrac{3}{13},\dfrac{4}{13},\dfrac{12}{13}\right)$. (B)
